content: Wise men speak because they have something to say; fools because they have to say something.
author: Plato
story:
Deeply traumatized by the Athenian democracy's unjust execution of his beloved teacher Socrates, Plato abandoned political ambitions to establish the Academy, the Western world's first institution of higher learning. Through immortal dramatic dialogues, he pointed humanity beyond the shadows of subjective opinion toward transcendent objective truth, justice, and beauty.

In formulating this reflection, Plato stripped away superficial conventions to address the core anatomy of silence. For Plato, true wisdom is never an abstract luxury, but an urgent practical discipline required to navigate life with clarity and unshakeable dignity.
